sources.title: OWASP Top 10:2025
sources.description: Current full release. Announced at OWASP Global AppSec Washington D.C., November 2025; final published text released January 2026 New: A03:2025 Software Supply Chain Failures, A10:2025 Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions. SSRF folded into A01 Broken Access Control; A09 renamed Security Logging and Alerting Failures. Supersedes the 2021 edition.

sources.title: SLSA Framework
sources.description: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts — graduated framework for build provenance and artifact integrity. Current spec: v1.1 (April 2025). Three-level Build track (L1–L3); Source and Dependencies tracks under development. v1.0 documentation still referenced in many tools — map L4 (legacy) to Build L3.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 (2021, superseded)
sources.description: Superseded by OWASP Top 10:2025. Retained only as an ID alias: many scanner rule-packs still emit 2021 category tags pending updates — map 2021 IDs to their 2025 equivalents (see references/owasp-top-10-coverage.md).

sources.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard (ASVS) 5.0
sources.description: ASVS 5.0.0 released May 30, 2025. First major update since 4.0 (2019). ~350 requirements across 17 chapters; expanded API, SPA, and microservice coverage; action-oriented requirements; clarifies that black-box testing alone is insufficient for most controls. Supersedes ASVS 4.0.3.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
sources.description: Separate from LLM Top 10. Announced 2025-12-09 (OWASP GenAI Security Project, Black Hat Europe / OWASP Agentic Security Summit); officially released. Ten categories, prefix ASI01-ASI10: planning, tool use, identity, supply chain, code execution, memory, inter-agent communication, cascading failures, human-agent trust, rogue agents.

sources.title: OpenGrep
sources.description: Community fork of Semgrep Community Edition (LGPL-2.1), launched January 2025 after Semgrep moved cross-function taint analysis to its commercial platform. Backed by Aikido, Endor Labs, Jit, Orca Security. Fully backward-compatible with Semgrep rule format, JSON, and SARIF output. No paid tier.

sources.title: Trivy Supply Chain Compromise Advisory (2026-03-19)
sources.description: GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23 / CVE-2026-33634. 2026-03-19: with compromised credentials an attacker published a malicious Trivy v0.69.4, force-pushed 76 of 77 version tags in aquasecurity/trivy-action and replaced all 7 tags in aquasecurity/setup-trivy. 2026-03-22: malicious Trivy v0.69.5 and v0.69.6 images were pushed to Docker Hub. Root cause: non-atomic credential rotation after a 2026-03-01 disclosure. Advisory's known-safe versions: Trivy v0.69.2 or v0.69.3, trivy-action 0.35.0, setup-trivy v0.2.6; images by digest and source builds were not affected. Guidance: rotate secrets exposed to affected pipelines, check for a tpcp-docs repository, pin actions to full commit SHAs.

sources.title: CVSS v4.0 (FIRST.org)
sources.description: Versioned CVSS specification. CNAs may supply v3.1, v4.0 or both. Read the CVE record and NIST NVD operations guidance for the enrichment policy in force before choosing score provenance; missing NVD enrichment is not evidence of low risk. Severity bands are unchanged from v3.1, but the vector-to-score computation differs: do not compare v3.1 and v4.0 scores directly.

sources.title: EPSS - Exploit Prediction Scoring System (FIRST.org)
sources.description: FIRST.org SIG. Current model: EPSS v4 (model version 2025.03.14). Estimates the probability that a published CVE will be exploited in the wild in the next 30 days. It is a forecast, not confirmation of exploitation; use CISA KEV for confirmed exploitation. FIRST publishes no action threshold: the 0.7/0.3 cut-offs in this skill are org policy aligned with software-security-appsec.

sources.title: Betterleaks
sources.description: Open-source secrets scanner created 2026-02-03 by the original gitleaks author as gitleaks' de facto successor; co-maintained with long-time gitleaks contributors. Reached v1.1.1 by 2026-03-17 and v1.1.2 by 2026-04-08. gitleaks itself is now feature-complete (security patches only). Betterleaks is young (weeks old at last check) — pilot it alongside gitleaks rather than replacing gitleaks outright until it has a longer track record in your CI.

sources.title: NIST: NVD operations update (2026-04-15)
sources.description: Historical announcement: from 2026-04-15 NVD prioritised enrichment of CVEs in CISA KEV, CVEs for software used in the federal government and critical software under EO 14028. Other CVEs are 'Lowest Priority - not scheduled for immediate enrichment'. NIST no longer routinely provides its own score where the CNA supplied one. Backlogged CVEs published before 2026-03-01 moved to 'Not Scheduled'. Check https://www.nist.gov/itl/nvd for the policy in force before interpreting an enrichment status.

sources.title: CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog
sources.description: Catalog of CVEs with confirmed exploitation in the wild. Used as the triage override in this skill and in vuln_tracker.py.

sources.title: actions/attest
sources.description: Generates signed provenance, SBOM or custom attestations. Since v4, actions/attest-build-provenance is a wrapper around it; new work should use actions/attest. Private/internal repos need GitHub Enterprise Cloud; not supported on GHES.

sources.title: Cosign 2.0 release notes
sources.description: Cosign 2.0 (2023-02-23) made keyless signing the default: COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 is no longer required. Verification requires --certificate-identity and --certificate-oidc-issuer.

metadata.title: QA Security Testing - Sources
metadata.description: Automated security testing pipelines for SAST, DAST, SCA, secret scanning, and container scanning. Use when integrating security scanners into CI, triaging findings, setting vulnerability SLAs, or building security regression tests.

game_theory_security_testing.title: Tambe — Security and Game Theory (2011)
game_theory_security_testing.description: Stackelberg security game formalism with ARMOR (LAX) and IRIS (port) deployed systems. Foundation for scan-scheduling-as-security-game and red-team Stackelberg models.

game_theory_security_testing.title: Sandler & Arce — Terrorism and Game Theory (Simulation & Gaming 2003)
game_theory_security_testing.description: Attacker cost-benefit and timing models. Applicable to exploitation-window analysis and dependency scan cadence decisions (P4).

game_theory_security_testing.title: Gordon & Loeb — Economics of Information Security Investment (ACM TISSEC 2002)
game_theory_security_testing.description: Single-period model of optimal information-security investment. game-theory-applied.md applies it per scan cycle as a heuristic (P4); it is not a repeated-game result.

game_theory_security_testing.title: MITRE ATT&CK Framework
game_theory_security_testing.description: Canonical tactic and technique taxonomy for red-team exercise scoring (R3) and ATT&CK coverage metric in anti-pattern A2.

game_theory_security_testing.title: CISA / MITRE ATT&CK Adversary Emulation Plans
game_theory_security_testing.description: Operationalized emulation plans grounding attacker behavior models used in red-team Stackelberg framing (P3) and scan scheduling (P1).

game_theory_security_testing.title: AFL++ Coverage-Guided Fuzzer
game_theory_security_testing.description: AFL++ project (community fork of AFL). Coverage-guided fuzzing feedback loop; the multi-armed bandit analogy in P2 and R2 is the skill's framing, not an AFL++ claim.
